title: Sampling Shepherd for Cache Policy Canary and Auto-Reverter
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, production-safe 'Sampling Shepherd' that orchestrates staged canaries of KV/prefix caching policy changes (TTL, key normalization, prefix-slicing, and batching hints). The shepherd will run targeted sample traffic to new cache configs, evaluate a set of statistical safety signals (latency, token-cost-per-request, cache hit uplift, error spike, and response-quality regressions), and either promote the policy, escalate it for manual review, or trigger an automated rollback (auto-reverter) when predefined safety gates are violated.

This ticket encapsulates design + MVP implementation for the shepherd, the canary sampling harness, observability checks, and the auto-reverter workflow. Emphasis is on conservative defaults, reproducible offline sims, and easy configuration by SRE/Platform teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sampling Shepherd service deployed in staging that can apply a caching config to 5% of traffic for a given model-route; 2) Statistical safety checks implemented: rolling 10-minute p95 latency delta, token-cost change, hit-rate lift, and KL divergence of response-token distributions; 3) Auto-reverter triggers rollback automatically when any safety gate breaches with configurable hysteresis; 4) Runbook + dashboard tiles added to Console showing canary cohort metrics and reversion events; 5) End-to-end e2e test simulating a spike in cache miss rate results in auto-reverter activation in CI.
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Runtime, and Product. Agreed safety gates and initial sampling fraction (5%).
2026-02-24: PoC sampling harness implemented in the request router (shadow routing mode). Running shadow samples against candidate TTL sets. Added synthetic workload generator.

2026-03-02: First offline simulations executed using production traces (24h) — validated hit-rate uplift predictions and cost delta estimate model. Identified corner case for short-lived prefixes causing noisy hit-rate signal.

2026-03-07: Implemented KL divergence-based response-quality monitor to detect distributional regressions from model-level reranking changes. Added 2-minute smoothing window for p95 latency to avoid flapping.

2026-03-10: Canary orchestration API v0.1 merged (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421). Staging shepherd deployed behind feature flag. Observability dashboards added (console tile: canary/sampling-shepherd).
decisions: Use sampling fraction default 5% with linear ramp to 20% for promotion; this balances statistical power with risk exposure.
Safety gates: p95 latency delta > +25ms OR token-cost increase > +7% OR hit-rate drop > -3% OR KL(response distribution) > 0.04 -> trigger rollback. Thresholds are configurable per-team.
Adopt KL divergence on token-prob distributions (rounded to 10 bins) rather than per-token equality to detect meaningful output drift while being robust to harmless variability.
Auto-reverter requires two sequential breach windows (2 consecutive 10-minute windows) unless a single-window severity threshold is crossed (emergency threshold).
risks: Noisy metrics for very low-cardinality prefixes can produce false positives -> mitigated by minimum-sample-size guard and adaptive smoothing.
Aggressive TTL increases may shift load patterns downstream (burst to origin or retrained model cache miss) causing downstream cost spikes; we need end-to-end cost view in canary checks.
Incorrect key-normalization rules could cause cache collisions across tenants -> require whitelist testing and per-tenant dry-run mode.
Auto-revert flapping if thresholds are too tight -> implement hysteresis and minimum stable-period before promotion.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): run shepherd in shadow/sampling mode with synthetic and production-like traffic for 2 weeks. Phase 2 (internal): enable canary for non-critical routes at 5% traffic for a set of observed-stable models; monitor for 7 days. Phase 3 (gradual): expand to more routes with ramp to 20% and enable auto-reverter with conservative thresholds. Phase 4: iterate thresholds and enable per-customer config. Each phase has a rollback dry-run and a manual kill-switch for 1-click abort.
test_plan: - Unit tests for statistical checks (KL, p95 delta, cost delta) - Integration tests with router shadowing and canary fractional routing - CI job that runs a synthetic miss-spike scenario and expects auto-reverter to fire - Load test to ensure shepherd itself adds <1% CPU overhead to router nodes - Chaos test that simulates metrics pipeline lag and verifies hysteresis prevents false rollback
metrics: Monitored metrics (Console): canary_hit_rate_change, canary_p95_latency_delta_ms, canary_token_cost_delta_pct, canary_response_kl, canary_samples_per_min, auto_reverts_count, promotion_success_rate. Alert conditions: auto_reverts_count > 0 for same route in 24h -> paging. Cost SLO: no canary should increase host-level token cost by >10% for a 24h window.
implementation_notes: Shepherd is implemented as small coordinator service that: 1) accepts a 'policy bundle' (TTL map, key-normalization rules, batching-hints); 2) instructs router to route N% to a canary cohort; 3) collects canary vs baseline metrics and runs checks; 4) writes audit events and triggers promotion/rollback. Use existing audit log sink (gs://redwood-logs/canary) and trace ids for debugging. Configs stored in ConfigStore with versioning and immutable bundle ids. PR referenced for core change: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/2187.
playbook: If a canary breach occurs: 1) auto-reverter will rotate cohort back to baseline and mark bundle as 'reverted' with reason; 2) shepherd posts incident note to Slack #runtime-canary and attaches last 60m graphs; 3) SRE on-call gets paged if revert count > 1 for same route; 4) open follow-up ticket with sanitized input samples for model/feature engineers.
runbook_snippet:
- To start a canary: curl -X POST https://shepherd.internal/api/v1/canaries -d '{
  "route": "/v1/generate/model-abc",
  "bundle_id": "bundle_20260305_02",
  "fraction": 0.05,
  "duration_min": 60
}'
- To force-promote: POST /api/v1/canaries/:id/promote - requires SRE token
- To force-revert: POST /api/v1/canaries/:id/revert
example_cache_key_guidelines: Prefer stable prefixing: <customer_id>:<model>:<input-shape-signature>. Normalize whitespace and truncate user-provided IDs to avoid high-cardinality keys. Avoid including ephemeral request ids or timestamps. Example rule set: 1) Lowercase, strip punctuation; 2) Replace user text blocks with 64-bit fingerprint; 3) Keep first-2 tokens of free-form prompt as part of shard key only for prompt-grouped routes.
simulation_notes: Offline sim harness uses a two-step approach: (A) replay sampled traffic (1% sample) against candidate policy to predict hit-rate uplift and tail latency impact, (B) run bootstrap resampling to estimate confidence intervals for hit-rate change. We use Bayesian shrinkage priors for low-sample prefixes to avoid overconfident uplift estimates.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on: 1) correctness of statistical gate thresholds and whether we should use KL vs JS divergence; 2) any missing privacy concerns in sampling (avoid sampling PII in exported artifacts); 3) the default hysteresis settings to prevent flapping. Requested reviewers: Priya Rao (SRE), Linh Tran (Runtime), Marcus Lee (Product).
